SHRI DINESH KOSHAL - ADVOCATE FOR THE RESPONDENT NO.3.
 NONE FOR THE RESPONDENT NO.1 AND 2.
 ORDER
With the consent of both learned counsel for the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal has been filed by the claimants/appellants under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 11.05.2007 passed in MVC.No.111/2006 by the Additional M.A.C.T., Jabalpur, seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that Tribunal has determined deceased's income as Rs.15,000/- per annum.

Learned counsel for the appellants, after referring to para 25 of the impugned award, submits that from evidence on record, it is clearly established that deceased was earning Rs. 100/- per day by working as Palledar.
On above grounds, it is urged that compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company submits that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
He further submits that present case relates to the year 2006.
Therefore, appellants are not entitled to receive consortium at the rate of Rs. 40,000/- and funeral expenses and loss of estate of Rs. 15,000/-.
Case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, AIR 2017 SC 5157 is of the year of 2017.

entities.text: Case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also urged that in the instant case,
deceased was travelling in goods vehicle as gratuitous passenger.
Therefore, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
On the above grounds, it is urged that no enhancement is required.
Hence, appeal filed by the appellants be dismissed.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.

6. So far as income of deceased is concerned, it is correct that applicant witness Kusum Bai has deposed in her testimony that her husband was working as Palledar and thereby earning Rs. 100/-
per day.
Perusal of deposition of Kusum and averments of claim petition reveals that therein it is mentioned that deceased was working as Palledar with owner of the offending vehicle Ashish Jain at Jhalon.

Claimants have not examined Ashish Jain or any person on behalf of the Ashish Jain to prove the fact that deceased was working as Palledar with Ashish Jain and Ashish Jain used to pay him Rs. 100/- per day and Rs. 50 as dietary allowance.

Therefore, in this Court's opinion from evidence on record, it is not established that deceased was working as Palledar with Ashish Jain and thereby earning Rs. 3000/- per months and Rs. 50/- per day as dietary allowance.

7. It is correct that in the instant case, accident occurred in the year 2006 and case of Smt. Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, AIR 2009 SC 3104, is of the year 2009 and case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) is of the year 2017.

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, AIR 2009 SC 3104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in M.A. Murthy Vs. State of Karnataka and other, AIR 2003 SC 3821, it cannot be said that principle laid down in Sarla Verma (supra) and Pranay Sethi (supra) would not apply to the fact of instant case.

entities.text: M.A. Murthy Vs. State of Karnataka and other, AIR 2003 SC 3821

sentences.text: Hence, submissions of learned counsel of the respondent No.3 are negated.

In the instant case,
no cross objections/separate appeal has been filed on behalf of the insurance company.

Therefore,
in the instant appeal, which has been filed by the claimants for enhancement of compensation,
insurance company is not entitled to challenge tribunal's findings with respect to liability to pay the compensation.
8. On the date of accident, minimum wages of an unskilled labour were Rs. 2427/- per month as notified under Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, deceased's monthly income is determined as Rs.
per month

. 
9. In the instant case, at the time of accident, deceased was aged 30 years.
Therefore, in view of age of deceased, 40% is to be added as future prospects and multiplier of 18 is to be applied.
Further, in view of number of dependent, 1/3 is to be deducted for personal and living expenses.
Further, except brother of deceased, three appellants are entitled to receive Rs.40,000/- as consortium.

Further,
appellants are also entitled to receive Rs.15,000/- for loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses.

10. Hence, in view of above, compensation is recalculated as under:-

Annual loss of dependency-(monthly loss of dependency x Rs. 27,168/-

5. Total loss of dependency-(Annual loss of dependency x Rs. 4,89,024/-
18 Multiplier)
6. Compensation for loss of spousal/parental/filial consortium Rs.1,20,000 /-
7. Compensation for loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
8. Compensation towards funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
9.

TOTAL COMPENSATION- Rs. 6,39,024/-

Other findings of the Tribunal shall remain intact.
13.
Appeal filed by the appellants is partly allowed to the extent as indicated above & disposed of accordingly.
